items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: something like the Louis Jordan shuffle rhythm type of thing

ctx.x: When I left home he was not playing music, no, he wasn't. He wasn't playing nor was my brother Charlie. I think I mentioned him, too. Charlie was a younger brother. Joe went into music after I left home, and he was very good. He almost was self taught, really, but he studied. He did do some studying, and he had a little group at home in Lake Charles, that is, and he played with little groups around

there, and finally, when he came out to California, then he got -- did manage to get in contact with some of the people that he knew, some of the musicians that he had met, and in their travels, you know, coming through Louisiana. And he did very, very well, and then he did do some things for Capitol on his own. "Rocking Boogie," was one, and he did a thing called, "Mardi Gras," and several other things that did very well. Well, he was somewhat ahead of his time, you know, because this was -- at that time it was…
But later something happened, I don't know, he just decided that he wanted to -- he didn't want to do it anymore. He just went into the religious vein.
